facts.fact: Guinea-Bissau's customs directorate reviewed with an African Development Bank mission on 2026-10-08 its migration from SYDONIA++ to SYDONIA World, which the mission head said had passed 80% execution, with the remaining applications and modules still to be installed.

UNCTAD's ASYCUDA Programme reports ASYCUDAWorld operational across all computerised customs offices, including the Port of Bissau, Bissau International Airport and the Sao Domingos, Gabu and Bafata offices, after migration from ASYCUDA++.

note: Participant only; no customs system status stated.

facts.fact: The Guinea-Bissau customs administration says it officially launched an air electronic manifest module in SYDONIA World on 17 September 2026, built with IATA, to receive advance cargo information.

The Direcao-Geral das Alfandegas' service order GDGA 10/26 says declarations are registered in SYDONIA World and its ASYVal valuation module takes effect on 1 May 2026, with value alerts resolved in the system before clearance.

note: A needs assessment for a maritime single window at the port, not a customs system or trade single window in service.

facts.fact: The customs directorate says Guinea-Bissau formally presented SYDONIA World, migrating from SYDONIA++, with training of customs staff under way.

note: ECOWAS says SIGMAT is not yet functional in Guinea-Bissau; no customs value fits.
A delegate called for SIGMAT to be extended to this country; no statement of its customs processing is given.
System claim held; a 'No' on the single window is not a value the study holds.
